title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E526 studies transverse vibrations of elastic rods. The Euler–Bernoulli equation is separated as y = C sin(ζ + t·ω²c√(2gb)/a²)·U(u), with u the dimensionless abscissa along the rod. This page treats the second case: one end free, the other 'simpliciter fixa' (simply supported or pinned). The previous page reduced the boundary conditions to tan ω = tanh ω = (e^ω − e^(−ω))/(e^ω + e^(−ω)). It also showed that there is no positive root in the first quadrant or in any even quadrant. (The trivial root ω = 0, rigid rotation about the pin, is tacitly discarded.) In the third quadrant Euler set ω = π + π/4 − Φ, which gives tan Φ = e^(−2ω) ≈ 1/2576, so Φ is under one arc-minute.

§25 (Cor. 2): the same holds, even more accurately, in later odd quadrants. The roots are ω ≈ 2π + π/4, 3π + π/4, 4π + π/4, 5π + π/4, …, i.e. ω_n ≈ (4n+1)π/4. This is the standard asymptotic root formula of tan x = tanh x. The exact first root is 3.9266 against 5π/4 = 3.92699, and the error decays like e^(−2ω).

§26 (Cor. 3): the roots are 5π/4, 9π/4, 13π/4, 17π/4, …. The simple tones are ω²c√(2gb)/a² divided by π, i.e. Euler counts single swings (half periods), as he does elsewhere. This gives (25, 81, 169, 289)·πc√(2gb)/(16a²), proportional to the squares of the odd numbers 5, 9, 13, 17. So the partials are inharmonic, in the ratio (4n+1)². Fundamental to first overtone is 25:81 = 1 : 3.24 ≈ 1 : 3¼. Musically 81/25 = 2 · (8/5) · (81/80): an octave plus a minor sixth, raised by exactly one syntonic comma. Euler names the tone 'gis' above C, 'exceeding it by one comma', and calls the combined sound 'parum grata' (not very pleasing).

§27 begins comparing this fundamental with the free–free fundamental 9πc√(2gb)/(4a²) = 36πc√(2gb)/(16a²). On the next page this gives the ratio 25:36, a just 'false fifth' (36/25).
errors: §25 says 'quartum quadrantem' for the root near 2π + 45° = 9π/4. That angle lies in the fifth quadrant (2π to 5π/2). The fourth quadrant (3π/2 to 2π) has negative tangent and, by Euler's own preceding argument, contains no root. It should read 'quintum'; the sequence 7th, 9th, 11th quadrants that follows is correct.
§26 'Cum igitur sit ϱ = π/4' is inconsistent with ϱ denoting the right angle (ϱ = π/2). It should read ½ϱ = π/4 (or ϱ = π/2). The subsequent values are correct.

The frequency expressions (25π…/16aa rather than 25π²…/16aa) are not an error. They follow Euler's convention of counting simple vibrations (angular frequency/π), consistent with the free–free value 9π/4 on the next page.

Musical labelling is slightly loose. The ratio 81/50 above the lower octave is exactly a syntonic comma above the just minor sixth 8/5 (as). Relative to Euler's own just gis = 25/16, the excess would be the great diesis 648/625, not a comma. The 'one comma' statement is exact only if 'gis' is read as the 8/5 key.
The zero root ω = 0 (rigid-body rotation about the pinned end) is silently excluded; harmless for acoustics.

ideas.what: Asymptotic location of roots of tan ω = tanh ω: ω_n ≈ (4n+1)π/4 with exponentially small correction tan Φ = e^(−2ω)
ideas.modern_name: Eigenvalues of the pinned–free (equivalently clamped–pinned) Euler–Bernoulli beam; asymptotic root approximation of a transcendental frequency equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E526) and the earlier Euler/D. Bernoulli beam work; standard in Rayleigh, Theory of Sound
ideas.where_published: E526 itself (Acta Acad. Petrop. 1779/1782); cf. Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II 11/2)

ideas.what: Overtones of the pinned–free rod are inharmonic, proportional to the squares of 5, 9, 13, 17, …
ideas.modern_name: Inharmonic partial series of a vibrating bar
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli and Euler (1740s), verified experimentally by Chladni
ideas.where_published: E526; earlier free–free and clamped results in Euler's Additamentum De curvis elasticis (E65, 1744) and D. Bernoulli's papers of 1741–43

ideas.what: Musical evaluation of the interval between fundamental and first overtone (81/25 ≈ octave + minor sixth + comma) and between different boundary conditions (25:36 false fifth)
ideas.modern_name: Acoustic interpretation of bar eigenfrequency ratios in just intonation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler / D. Bernoulli; later Chladni's experiments
ideas.where_published: E526; Euler's musical theory in the Tentamen (E33)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine corollaries of a well-known paper, already covered by Truesdell's historical commentary on elastic rods. The only points of note are a minor quadrant mislabel, a ϱ typo, and the observation that 81/50 is exactly a comma above 8/5.
transcription_corrections: Long s is rendered as 'f' throughout: 'finus/cofinus/fit/feptimo/nancifcimur/fuppeditat/foni/fimplices/fequentibus/cenfetur/fecundus/fimul/feu/fonus/fuperabit/ficque/exiftet/grauiffimus' should read 'sinus/cosinus/sit/septimo/nanciscimur/suppeditat/soni/simplices/sequentibus/censetur/secundus/simul/seu/sonus/superabit/sicque/existet/grauissimus'.
In §25 the word is 'Pergamus igitur ad quartum quadrantem' (as printed; the original has 'quartum', an error in Euler's text, not the transcription).

'quem tamen sonum vno commate superabit' corresponds to the image's hyphenated 'so-/fundamentalis' line break. The printed text appears garbled ('so- fundamentalis fuerit'), but the meaning is unchanged.
